messages:
deploy-bot: Planned change window: 2026-04-10 04:00-05:15 UTC. Scope: hosted API (generation + embeddings) in ap-southeast-1 and us-east-1. Actions: runtime image roll (v2.4.0), model catalog metadata refresh, and release-notes publish. Rolling by AZs, pause autoscale during window.

Rita (prodops): Need customer-facing artifacts: concise statuspage entry, a short email for opt-in customers (and a one-line SMS for ops-critical customers), plus public release notes blurb. Drafts pls — we send status T-60.

Omar (eng-oncall): Impact summary: rolling drains will cause intermittent 502/503s up to ~45s per drained instance. We expect small p95 spikes during canary. Canary plan: 10% traffic in ap-southeast-1 for 15m, then ramp if metrics ok. If canary fails, we pin to runtime v2.3.x and open incident channel. No expected data-plane schema changes.

Sam (support): I'll prepare canned replies: retry/backoff guidance, when to contact SC, and a snippet telling Dedicated customers they're not affected unless using managed autoscaler. Also include a short escalation email for enterprise contacts.

Priya (sre): Rollback/abort conditions: sustained 5xx >3% for 10m during any ramp, p95 >400ms for 20m, or any kernel OOM/panic on >1 node. If triggered: stop rollout, re-route canaries to v2.3.x, and start rollback playbook. Post-change verification required before unpause autoscaling.

Rita (prodops): Draft statuspage snippet (compact):

"Scheduled maintenance: Runtime image roll and model catalog refresh for hosted API in ap-southeast-1 & us-east-1.
Start: 2026-04-10 04:00 UTC — End: 2026-04-10 05:15 UTC (approx).
Impact: Intermittent request failures (short 502/503) and transient latency increases during rolling drains.
Customer action: No action required. Dedicated/private deployments unaffected. Updates at status.redwood.ai."

Rita (prodops): Draft customer email (short):

Subject: Planned maintenance — brief disruption to hosted API in AP/US (Apr 10)

Body: Hi — We will perform scheduled maintenance on Apr 10 that may cause brief request failures or latency increases for hosted API users in AP-SOUTHEAST and US-EAST. No action needed. We expect service to return to normal within the window and will post live updates at status.redwood.ai. Contact support if you have specific SLAs to check.

Sam (support): SMS for ops-critical customers (one-liner):
"Planned maintenance Apr 10 04:00 UTC — brief hosted API interruptions possible in AP/US. See status.redwood.ai"

Rita (prodops): Release notes blurb (public):

"Runtime v2.4.0 rollout: improved KV-cache hit stability, kernel wiring fixes for long-context workloads, and model-catalog metadata sync optimizations. No API changes. Full notes: https://docs.redwood.ai/release-notes/2.4.0"

Omar (eng-oncall): Canary metrics to watch: 5xx rate, p50/p95 latency, token-per-request throughput, KV cache hit ratio, and tail latencies for long-context requests. Thresholds: 5xx >1% during canary = investigate; >3% = abort.

Priya (sre): Post-maint checklist (must pass before unpause):
1) Synthetic generation and embedding hits succeed across regions.
2) p50/p95 within 15% of baseline.
3) No increase in kernel exceptions in last 30m.
4) Autoscaling resumed and behaves within expected target utilization.

Sam (support): I'll stage the statuspage update in drafts and queue the email. Also preparing a short "What we changed" FAQ for customers who ask about performance differences post-update.

Rita (prodops): Thanks team. Omar — can you confirm the canary start time (T+30) and set the rollout automation to pause for manual check at 10% and 50% ramps?

Omar (eng-oncall): Affirmative. Canary start in 30m. Rollout automation set to pause at 10% and 50% for 15m each for metric checks. Notifying eng-oncall and support channels.

deploy-bot: Canary initiated. Monitoring hooks live. Notifying #eng-oncall and #support.
